Plot zero patterns

Source: R/coda_diagnostics.r
plot.ecodive_zero_pattern.Rd

Draws a zero_pattern() result: the most frequent patterns as rows, the features that are sometimes zero as columns, zeros dark; with each feature's percentage of zeros above, and each pattern's percentage of the samples on the right.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ecodive_zero_pattern'
plot(x, n_patterns = 30, n_features = 50, ...)

Arguments

x

A result of zero_pattern().

n_patterns

The number of patterns to draw, the most frequent first. Default 30. Inf or TRUE for all.

n_features

The largest number of features to draw. Default 50. Inf or TRUE for all.

...

Passed on to graphics::image(); main and sub replace the title and subtitle.

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

Features drawn. Only features that are zero in some samples but not all: those never zero and those always zero say nothing about patterns, and are counted in the subtitle instead. When more than n_features remain, those whose proportion of zeros is closest to one half are drawn, as the most informative. Columns are sorted by their proportion of zeros, the fewest on the left.

Patterns drawn. The n_patterns most frequent, top to bottom. Patterns are defined on all the features, so two rows can look the same when they differ only in features that aren't drawn; the subtitle says how many are hidden.

When nearly every sample has its own pattern, as in most microbiome tables, the top bars (each feature's zeros) are the useful part.

See also

zero_pattern(), replace_zeros(), structural_zeros().

Examples

    plot(zero_pattern(ex_counts), n_features = 20)
